Week 25 Appendix: The Week Power Accumulated Quietly

Executive discretion widened, enforcement hardened, and dissent grew costlier while a hollowed disaster response killed dozens in Texas.

This was a high-pressure week for democratic structure, defined less by a single rupture than by the convergence of executive aggrandizement, politicized enforcement, and institutional hollowing. The strongest pattern was the use of formal state power to weaken checks: the Supreme Court limited nationwide injunctions and cleared mass federal layoffs, while the administration blocked congressionally approved funds, constrained information to Congress, and continued asserting unilateral authority in trade, war, and immigration. A second major theme was coercive immigration governance: TPS terminations, third-country deportations, militarized raids, masked agents, and expanded ICE funding all pushed toward a stratified citizenship regime enforced through intimidation. Third, the week exposed administrative degradation in public safety and expertise, especially through FEMA and National Weather Service failures during the Texas floods and RFK Jr.’s purge of vaccine expertise. Courts still provided some pockets of resistance, especially on birthright citizenship and Florida’s immigration law, but the net effect of the week was to deepen executive leverage, weaken neutral administration, and normalize retaliation, spectacle, and selective legality as governing methods.

  8. President Trump limited the classified information shared with Congress: Restricting lawmakers' access to classified material weakened oversight of executive actions and national security decisions. (2025-07-06)

  4. Robert F. Kennedy Jr. spread misinformation about measles vaccines and vaccine-related autism claims: False claims from a cabinet official distorted the public information environment around vaccination and public health. (2025-07-07) [single source]
  5. Amazon used referral fee incentives to encourage favorable Prime Day media coverage: Pay-linked promotion blurred the line between journalism and advertising, weakening independent consumer information. (2025-07-08) [single source]
  6. The FCC sought comments on its anti-harassment intake form information collection: The notice concerned internal reporting systems that support accountability and recordkeeping inside a federal agency. (2025-07-09)
